title: test(console): parity ledger reads a retirement from the spec, and no older reason may hide one (objectui#10033)
body:
Fixes #10033
Clause-②: no

## The card's question, answered from the test's own population logic

**Is the waiver population derived from the spec at all?** Yes. And retired keys are **in** it, in a special form. That makes this case (b) of the dispatch.

- **Population.** `covered`, `registeredWithoutInputs` and `accounts for every spec-carried block` all start from `Object.keys(ComponentPropsMap)`. The partition test requires `covered` ∪ `registeredWithoutInputs` ∪ `UNJUDGED_SPEC_BLOCKS` to equal that set exactly, with each block counted once.
- **A stale waiver (a key outside the population) is already caught, in two places.** The first is the partition's converse (`accounted for a block ComponentPropsMap does not carry`). The second is the ledger rot check (`is ledgered but the spec no longer carries it — delete the entry`). So this PR adds no new tripwire for that case.
- **Retired keys stay in the population, because the spec keeps their rows on purpose.** The row is one of the retirement's refusal doors. Readings from the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 (lockfile-resolved), taken at base `ea02938cd`, using the `@object-ui/test-support` tombstone judge:

| type | in `PageComponentType` | in `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES` | row keys listed / tombstoned / authorable | empty bag parses |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `user:profile` | no | **yes** | 0 / 0 / 0 (`z.never`) | refused |
| `element:form` | no | no | 6 / 6 / 0 | accepted |
| `element:filter` | no | no | 6 / 6 / 0 | accepted |
| controls: `cloud-connection:panel`, `marketplace:installed-list`, `mcp:connect-agent` | no | no | 0 / 0 / 0 | accepted |

Three things follow from that reading:

- **Mechanism assumption 3 is half false.** `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES` has exactly one member, `user:profile`. `element:form` left `PageComponentType` through the **element-grain** retirement (objectstack#9249, listed in the spec's 17.3.0 changelog), not through that table. `element:filter` left the same way earlier (objectstack#9220, 17.1.0). So "read the spec's retired set" as that table alone would not cover `element:form`.
- **Excluding retired rows from the population is the wrong way round.** A registration of a retired type in this repo would drop out of `covered` together with its row, and nothing would judge it. objectui#8176 built this ledger to end exactly that absence. With the rows kept in, such a registration is judged (every input it publishes is off-spec) and is also counted twice, which the partition refuses.
- **Both waiver reasons the card names are false today.** `user:profile` is false in both halves, as the card measured. `element:form` cites a `block-types.ts` palette exclusion that says "no renderer — use the object-bound `object-form` block". That entry was deleted by commit `639114c4d`, the delivery of objectui#7122 through PR #7685. It now appears in that file only as a note that the type is RETIRED UPSTREAM.

## What changed (test-only, one file plus an empty changeset)

1. **`isRetiredUpstream(type)`** reads both of the spec's retirement spellings, and never a list kept here. A type counts as retired when it is out of `PageComponentType` **and** one of these holds:
   - it is named in `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES` (retired by name);
   - its row lists keys and every one of them is a tombstone (retired at element grain).

   Leaving the enum is required but is not enough on its own: the controls above are outside the enum too, and the predicate answers `false` for them.
2. **A third ledger class, `RETIRED UPSTREAM`.** The rot check asserts two things for it: `isRetiredUpstream(type)` is true, and the accepted key set is empty. If upstream restores the type or gives its row a key, the entry goes red.
3. **The class-closing guard.** An entry under `EMPTY SPEC SHAPE` or `NOT REGISTERED, DELIBERATELY` now fails when the spec retires its type. That is the check that stops a hand-written reason from outliving a retirement, which is what happened to both entries here.
4. **Entries rewritten.** `user:profile` and `element:form` now say what is true, citing the upstream ruling and landing (objectstack#14159, objectstack#15112, objectstack#9249) and the objectui-side reconciliation (objectui#7122).
   - ⚠️ `element:filter` moves too. This is an in-place fix under the same-class exemption, and I am naming it here because the claim's file surface names only the other two entries. It was retired at element grain by objectstack#9220 (17.1.0), and its `EMPTY SPEC SHAPE` reason never mentioned that. The new guard turns exactly that state red, so leaving it behind would not pass. It is the same file, the same defect class and the same gate, with nothing new to verify.
5. **The docblock** now has three classes (it said two) and a paragraph on why a retired block stays in the population.

The census does not move: `specCarried` 45, `judged` 29, `registeredPropless` 7, `ledgeredUnjudgeable` 9. It is the same nine entries under corrected reasons.

**Changeset.** The dispatch expected none. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` refused without one, because it counts any file under a released package's `src/`, test files included. So the PR adds `.changeset/10033-parity-ledger-retired-upstream.md` with an **empty frontmatter**, which declares that nothing is released. The gate now passes.

The second file is the only other test that reads this file, by content. | `Test Files 2 passed (2)` · `Tests 228 passed (228)` · `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| same parity file at base `ea02938cd`, before the edit (control: the stale reasons were green then) | `Tests 199 passed (199)` |

| eslint on the touched file (`apps/console`, the console's own `eslint .` config) | exit 0 · `--format json`: 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings. **This is a narrowing, with its evidence:** (1) the population comes from eslint's own config, where `isPathIgnored` is false for the test file and true for the changeset; (2) the file count comes from the JSON output; (3) type-aware linting is off (`calculateConfigForFile` shows no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch. |

objectui has no `dispatch-gates.mjs`. I derived the gate list by hand from `.github/workflows/*.yml`, keeping the gates whose scripts read test sources, `apps/console` or `.changeset/`. The full `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` shards are left to CI.

## Ablation: three legs, from the committed state

Each leg used `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, with the test running under the lock. I wrote down the expected result before each run: exactly one failed test, the rot check, naming the mutated type. The observed direction was red on all three, as expected.

| leg | mutation (landing proven: anchor count 1 → 0, blob changed) | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `user:profile` entry → its exact pre-fix text | `1 failed / 198 passed` · `user:profile is retired upstream, and its ledger reason does not say so — rewrite the entry as RETIRED UPSTREAM` |
| 2 | `element:form` entry → its exact pre-fix text | `1 failed / 198 passed` · `element:form is retired upstream, and its ledger reason does not say so …` |
| 3 | specificity control: `cloud-connection:panel` (outside the enum, empty shape, not retired) relabelled `RETIRED UPSTREAM` | `1 failed / 198 passed` · `cloud-connection:panel is ledgered as retired upstream, and the spec does not retire it …` |

Every restore was `git checkout HEAD --` on the absolute path, proven by blob == HEAD (`f714fdd786dc`), `git diff HEAD` empty and `git status --porcelain` empty. The control run at the base (199 passed) shows that legs 1 and 2 describe a state that was green before this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- Nothing is filed. There are no class a/b/c findings from this run.
- AGENTS.md #11 asks for opportunistic repair of cross-file `path:line` citations in a file you touch. This file has older ones, outside the ledger entries, and I left them alone because the claim's surface is the ledger. Nobody is carrying that repair.
- `ai:chat_window`'s `NOT REGISTERED, DELIBERATELY` reason was re-read against `placeholders.tsx` and `block-types.ts` and is still true. The new guard also passes for it.
